title: Data table / grid
use_when: Homogeneous records with several comparable attributes; sorting, filtering, selection, bulk actions, inline editing.
avoid_when: Fewer than ~10 rows (use a list), heterogeneous items (use cards/list), phone widths (convert to rows).
guidance: Sticky header, row height by density token, zebra striping optional (prefer hover/selection highlight), column resize/reorder/visibility persisted, sort indicator with aria-sort, selection checkbox column with header select-all and a count, row actions visible on focus as well as hover, inline edit with Enter/Escape, keyboard grid navigation (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/Down), virtualised rows, loading skeleton rows, empty state inside the table body. Financial tables: see numeric rule.

implementation.react: TanStack Table (headless) + TanStack Virtual; render semantic <table> when static, role=grid when interactive; sticky via position: sticky on th.
implementation.shadcn: DataTable recipe (TanStack) is the convention; keep the Table primitives, add virtualisation for >200 rows.
implementation.winui: CommunityToolkit DataGrid (keyboard + UIA built in) or ItemsView; avoid ListView with a fake header row.
implementation.wpf: DataGrid with virtualisation flags; DevExpress GridControl if present in the project.
implementation.avalonia: TreeDataGrid for large/hierarchical data, DataGrid otherwise.
implementation.compose: LazyColumn with a fixed header Row and horizontal scroll state shared by rows; on phones prefer list rows.

title: Form
use_when: Any data entry: settings, checkout, applications, record editing.
avoid_when: Batch entry of many similar rows (use a data-entry grid); single toggles (inline).
guidance: Labels above, help text below, required marked in text, field widths sized to content, grouped by section with headings, one column, inline validation on blur, error summary on submit with links to fields, primary action last (or sticky), unsaved-changes guard, autosave with status for long forms, autofill attributes. TV: one field per row, DOWN moves to next, system keyboard, minimal fields.

implementation.react: react-hook-form or native form + FormData; associate errors with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
implementation.shadcn: Form + FormField wrappers already wire labels/description/message ids.
implementation.compose: OutlinedTextField with supportingText/isError; imeAction Next/Done; Modifier.semantics for error.
implementation.swiftui: Form with Sections; TextField with .textContentType and .submitLabel.
implementation.winui: TextBox Header + PlaceholderText; InfoBar for summary; ValidationErrors via Community Toolkit or manual TextBlock linked by AutomationProperties.DescribedBy.
implementation.wpf: Binding with ValidatesOnNotifyDataErrors and an ErrorTemplate that shows text, not only a red border.

title: Dialog / modal
use_when: Confirmation, short focused task, blocking decision.
avoid_when: Long forms, content that users need to reference while working (use a panel), stacking dialogs, mobile (prefer sheets or full-screen), TV (prefer full-screen or side sheet with clear focus).
guidance: Title as heading, one primary action, safe default for destructive confirmations, focus management per dialog rule, sized to content with max width, scroll inside the body not the page, Escape and close button, backdrop click closes only for non-destructive dialogs. Mobile: bottom sheet or full-screen; TV: full-screen with first focus on the safe action.

implementation.react: <dialog> with showModal() or a tested library (Radix Dialog); never a div overlay with onClick.
implementation.shadcn: Dialog / AlertDialog / Sheet / Drawer chosen by task, not by look.
implementation.compose: AlertDialog / ModalBottomSheet; TV: androidx.tv.material3 has no dialog — use a full-screen composable with focusRequester.
implementation.winui: ContentDialog (one at a time) with DefaultButton set.
implementation.wpf: Owned Window with ShowDialog or a tested dialog service; set initial focus.

title: Drawer / side panel
use_when: Secondary detail or editing beside the main content (record details, filters, settings), non-blocking on wide screens.
avoid_when: As the primary navigation on desktop (use a rail), or for blocking confirmations.
guidance: Inline (pushes content) on wide screens, overlay on narrow; width from tokens (320–480 px); heading + close; focus moves in on open and returns on close; content scrolls independently; TV: side sheet that keeps the player/content visible and traps DPAD inside until BACK.

implementation.shadcn: Sheet (overlay) or a resizable panel for inline; not both for the same content.
implementation.compose: ModalNavigationDrawer / PermanentDrawerSheet; TV: androidx.tv.material3 NavigationDrawer or a custom Box with focusGroup.
implementation.swiftui: NavigationSplitView inspector / .inspector(isPresented:); tvOS: custom side sheet with .focusSection().

title: Menu / dropdown / context menu
use_when: Overflow actions, context actions on an object, account menus.
avoid_when: Navigation (use links/tabs), single actions (use a button), forms (use selects).
guidance: Opens on click/Enter/Space and on Shift+F10 / right-click for context menus, arrow keys move, type-ahead, Escape closes and restores focus, items are buttons/links with icons only where meaningful, destructive items separated at the end, disabled items stay visible with a reason, positions within the viewport. Mobile: bottom sheet or platform menu.

implementation.react: Radix/React Aria menu; never a div list with hover CSS.
implementation.shadcn: DropdownMenu / ContextMenu; keep shortcuts in DropdownMenuShortcut.
implementation.winui: MenuFlyout with KeyboardAccelerator on items; ContextFlyout on the element.
implementation.wpf: ContextMenu bound to commands; InputGestureText shows shortcuts.
implementation.compose: DropdownMenu anchored to the button; on TV avoid menus and use a full row of buttons or a side sheet.

title: Tabs
use_when: Peer views of the same object (Details / Activity / Files) at the same level.
avoid_when: Sequential steps (wizard), primary navigation on web (use nav), more than ~6 tabs (use a select or side nav), tabs that hide required form fields.
guidance: Tablist with roving tabindex (arrow keys switch, Tab moves into the panel), selected tab marked by more than colour, tab labels short, panel content lazy but state preserved, URL reflects the tab on web; TV: selection on focus with a delay or on SELECT (choose one, be consistent), DOWN enters content.

implementation.react: Radix Tabs / React Aria Tabs; sync with the router search param.
implementation.shadcn: Tabs primitive; sync value with URL via nuqs or router.
implementation.compose: TabRow/PrimaryTabRow + HorizontalPager; TV: androidx.tv.material3 TabRow with focusRestorer.
implementation.swiftui: Picker(.segmented) for ≤4 short options, otherwise a custom tab strip; tvOS TabView.
implementation.winui: TabView for document tabs, SelectorBar/NavigationView top for section tabs.

source: WAI-ARIA tabs; Material tabs; Windows SelectorBar

title: Sidebar / navigation rail
use_when: Justified by the left-rail navigation pattern (6+ sections, frequent switching).
avoid_when: Three destinations, marketing pages, phones (collapse to drawer), TV.
guidance: Grouped items with group labels, active item with indicator + aria-current, collapsible to icon rail with tooltips and accessible names, keyboard: Tab into the rail once then arrows, collapse state persisted, footer for account/settings, no more than two nesting levels; never a second rail for sub-navigation (use the content header).

implementation.shadcn: Sidebar component family; SidebarGroup for grouping; keep it at one instance per app.
implementation.winui: NavigationView with MenuItems + FooterMenuItems; PaneDisplayMode Auto.
implementation.wpf: ListBox styled as nav with a selection indicator; or a third-party NavigationView equivalent already in the project.
implementation.avalonia: SplitView + ListBox, or a NavigationView-like control from an existing dependency.

title: Command palette
use_when: Power-user tools with many commands and records; augments visible navigation.
avoid_when: As the only way to reach features; touch-first apps.
guidance: Global shortcut, combobox semantics (aria-activedescendant), grouped results (commands, records, navigation), recent items, fuzzy match with highlighted matches, keyboard hints, Escape restores focus, executes in ≤1 keystroke after selection, debounced async search with loading state.

implementation.shadcn: Command (cmdk) inside CommandDialog; register commands from one registry shared with menus.
implementation.react: cmdk or React Aria ComboBox; virtualise beyond ~500 items.
implementation.winui: AutoSuggestBox in a Flyout with grouped ItemsSource; KeyboardAccelerator Ctrl+K.

title: Search field and results
use_when: Catalogues, media libraries, admin lists, docs.
avoid_when: Tiny data sets where filtering chips suffice.
guidance: Prominent field with type=search, clear button, suggestions as a listbox with keyboard support, result count announced, query in the URL, recent searches, empty-result guidance, debounce. Mobile: full-screen search with the keyboard open and results as a list. TV: a dedicated search screen, system keyboard or voice, results in rails, focus returns to the field on BACK.

implementation.react: React Aria ComboBox / Radix + listbox; role=search landmark.
implementation.compose: SearchBar/DockedSearchBar; TV: TextField with keyboard + results LazyColumn of LazyRows.
implementation.swiftui: .searchable(text:) on the navigation stack; tvOS .searchable renders the system search screen.

title: Filter bar / faceted filters
use_when: Lists with several filterable attributes.
avoid_when: One or two filters (inline selects); TV (use rail categories or a simple filter row).
guidance: Desktop: filter row above the content with chips for applied filters; facets as popovers with checkboxes and counts; 'clear all'; results update with a count. Mobile: filter button with badge count opens a sheet; apply button; applied chips under the search field. Persist in URL.

implementation.shadcn: Popover + Command/Checkbox for facets; Badge for applied chips; nuqs for URL state.
implementation.compose: FilterChip / AssistChip row + ModalBottomSheet for full facets.
implementation.winui: CommandBar with AppBarToggleButton or a Flyout with CheckBox list.

title: Pagination vs infinite scroll vs load more
use_when: Any list longer than one screen.
avoid_when: Never use infinite scroll where the footer must be reachable or where users return to specific items (use pagination or load-more).
guidance: Tables and admin lists: numbered pagination with page size and total; feeds: load-more or infinite scroll with scroll restoration and a way to link to items; catalogues: load-more; TV rails: lazy append at the rail end. Pagination is a nav landmark with aria-current on the page.

title: Chart container and interaction
use_when: Any chart in a product.
avoid_when: Decorative charts with no question; charts of fewer than ~4 points (use a stat).
guidance: Title that states the question, unit and time range visible, legend as direct labels where possible, tooltip also keyboard-reachable (focusable points or a data table toggle), accessible summary text, consistent palette, responsive (reduce ticks, not data), empty/loading/error states, no animation beyond a single load transition and none on data refresh. Provide the data table or CSV.

implementation.react: Recharts/Visx/ECharts already in the project; add role=img + aria-label summary and a table fallback.
implementation.winui: LiveCharts2 / Syncfusion / DevExpress if present; otherwise Win2D drawing with an UIA-friendly table alongside.
implementation.compose: Vico or a Canvas; expose contentDescription summary.
implementation.swiftui: Swift Charts with .accessibilityLabel/.accessibilityValue per mark (built-in audio graph).

title: KPI / stat tile
use_when: Headline metrics on dashboards.
avoid_when: More than ~6 KPIs in a row (users stop reading); KPIs without context (no comparison, no unit).
guidance: Label, value with unit and tabular figures, comparison (vs previous period) with sign + arrow + colour, optional sparkline, consistent decimal precision, the most important KPI larger or first, no icon per tile unless it disambiguates, whole tile links to the detail. Avoid the 'four identical cards with big numbers and a gradient' default.

title: Media card (poster/thumbnail)
use_when: Items recognised by artwork in rails, grids, and continue-watching rows.
avoid_when: Text-recognised items; dense lists.
guidance: Fixed aspect, image with placeholder + title fallback, title below (1–2 lines, ellipsis), one status overlay max (progress bar, live badge, new), whole card is one focusable/tappable element with an accessible name (title + status), TV focus = scale + border/glow, hover on web = subtle lift, touch = pressed state; no inner buttons on TV.

implementation.compose-tv: androidx.tv.material3 Card/StandardCardContainer with scale/border in focused state.
implementation.react-native: Pressable + Image (expo-image) + Animated scale on focus; accessibilityLabel composed.
implementation.react: <a> or <button> wrapping the art; CSS :focus-visible and :hover transforms; loading=lazy below fold.

title: Player transport controls
use_when: Video/audio playback surfaces.
avoid_when: Never custom-build when the platform control set already meets the need and the brand allows it.
guidance: Play/pause, seek slider with time readout and keyboard/remote stepping, skip ±10 s, next/previous where relevant, captions and audio track selectors, quality only if user-facing, live indicator and go-to-live for live streams, volume on web/desktop only (TV uses the remote), controls overlay auto-hides except while focused/hovered; every control labelled; captions styling respects system preferences.

implementation.html-css: <video> + custom controls with role=slider for seek; media-chrome web components are a solid base.
implementation.compose-tv: Media3 with a Compose overlay; KEYCODE handling for media keys; focusRequester on play/pause.
implementation.react-native: react-native-video; TVEventHandler; overlay with Animated opacity.
implementation.swiftui: AVPlayerViewController on tvOS gives system transport UI with Siri Remote support; customise only if brand requires.

source: Android TV playback; tvOS HIG; media accessibility practice

title: TV rail (horizontal row of cards)
use_when: Categorised browsing on TV home, section, and search screens.
avoid_when: Fewer than ~4 items (use a grid row), comparison tasks.
guidance: Rail title (≥24 sp) left-aligned in the safe area, cards of one aspect ratio, focused card scrolls to a fixed pivot (~10–30% from left) with LEFT at index 0 going to navigation, focus memory per rail, lazy loading of items and images, 'see all' as the last card if the rail is capped, no wrap-around, consistent card counts per width (Android: ~4 landscape / ~6 portrait at 960 dp).

implementation.compose-tv: LazyRow inside LazyColumn with focusRestorer() and LocalBringIntoViewSpec for pivot; item keys stable; contentPadding = safe margins.
implementation.react-native: FlatList horizontal + TVFocusGuideView; getItemLayout for smooth scrolling; keep lastFocusedIndex ref.
implementation.react: Spatial navigation lib with per-row focus keys; scrollIntoView with block:'nearest' and a CSS scroll-padding-left for the pivot.

source: Android TV lists/rows; Compose for TV lists guide

title: EPG / programme guide
use_when: Live TV with many channels.
avoid_when: On-demand only catalogues; phones in portrait (use a per-channel list).
guidance: See the EPG grid pattern for structure; component specifics: cell shows title + time with ellipsis, minimum cell width so 5-minute programmes stay focusable (with a time label on focus), current programme highlighted and the 'now' line updates every minute, channel column sticky with logo + number, day picker above the grid, focus moves by programme not by pixel, long press or a key opens programme detail with record/remind actions, jump-to-now shortcut, mini preview of the focused channel optional.

implementation.compose-tv: Custom LazyLayout or LazyRow-of-LazyColumn sharing horizontal scroll; measure cells from time deltas; use Modifier.focusProperties to override up/down to the same time slot.
implementation.react: Virtualised absolute-positioned grid (Planby style); spatial navigation resolves by data (channel index, time) rather than DOM geometry.

title: Mobile list and swipe actions
use_when: Phone lists of homogeneous items.
avoid_when: Image-first browsing (grid), dense comparison (desktop table).
guidance: Row ≥48 dp / 44 pt, leading avatar/icon optional, title + secondary line, trailing meta or chevron, dividers or spacing, swipe actions with labelled buttons and a menu equivalent, pull-to-refresh where data is live, sticky section headers for grouped lists, lazy lists with stable keys, selection mode via long press with a visible toolbar.

implementation.compose: LazyColumn + ListItem; SwipeToDismissBox for swipe actions; stickyHeader for groups.
implementation.swiftui: List with .swipeActions and Sections; LazyVStack only when List styling is impossible.
implementation.react-native: FlatList with keyExtractor; Swipeable from gesture-handler.

title: Settings screen
use_when: Preferences, account, notifications, appearance.
avoid_when: Never bury frequently changed settings three levels deep; never use toggles for actions.
guidance: Grouped rows with clear labels and current values visible, toggles for booleans with immediate effect, pickers for enums, destructive actions at the end with confirmation, search for long settings, platform idiom (grouped lists on mobile, sections/panes on desktop, TV: vertical list with DPAD and a right-side value column). Save behaviour explicit (auto vs Save button).
source: Apple HIG settings; Material settings; Windows settings

title: Empty / zero state
use_when: First use, no results, cleared lists, error recovery.
avoid_when: Never a blank area; never a giant illustration that pushes the action below the fold.
guidance: Short heading stating the situation, one sentence of why/what next, one primary action (or none if nothing can be done), optional small meaningful illustration, same layout region as the content it replaces, and on TV a focusable action so focus is never lost.

title: Toast / snackbar / banner
use_when: Transient confirmation (saved, sent, undo), persistent info (banner), blocking errors (dialog, not toast).
avoid_when: Never put required actions only in a toast; never stack more than ~3; never auto-dismiss errors.
guidance: Toast: bottom (mobile) or bottom-left/top-right (desktop) consistent position, ≥5 s or until dismissed, undo where applicable, live region polite. Banner: inline at the top of the region it concerns, dismissible if non-critical. TV: brief overlay in the safe area that never steals focus.

implementation.shadcn: Sonner for toasts; Alert for inline banners.
implementation.compose: SnackbarHost with duration; TV: a custom overlay composable, no Snackbar (it steals no focus but positions badly).
implementation.swiftui: No system toast; use a lightweight overlay with .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently) announcement.
implementation.winui: InfoBar for inline; TeachingTip for contextual; app notifications for system-level.

title: Wizard / stepper
use_when: Ordered multi-step flows (checkout, applications, setup).
avoid_when: Independent sections (tabs); flows that fit one screen.
guidance: Step indicator with names and progress (list semantics, aria-current=step), Back never loses data, one primary action per step, review step before submit, resume support, each step a real page/route on web; TV: full-screen steps with default focus on the primary action.

title: Tree view
use_when: Hierarchies (folders, accounts, org units, categories) that users expand and select.
avoid_when: Flat lists; mobile (use drill-down lists).
guidance: Full APG tree semantics (roles tree/treeitem/group, aria-expanded, aria-level), arrow keys expand/collapse/move, type-ahead, multi-select with Shift/Ctrl where needed, lazy children with a loading indicator, virtualised for large trees, indentation lines optional but consistent, drag/drop with a keyboard alternative.

implementation.winui: TreeView (built-in UIA); TreeViewNode.HasUnrealizedChildren for lazy load.
implementation.wpf: TreeView with HierarchicalDataTemplate + virtualisation; DevExpress TreeListControl if present.
implementation.react: react-arborist or React Aria Tree; never nested <ul> with onClick only.

title: Data-entry grid (spreadsheet-like)
use_when: Batch entry of many similar rows (invoice lines, journal entries, stock counts).
avoid_when: Occasional single-record edits (use a form).
guidance: Enter/Tab move predictably (configurable), F2 edits, Escape cancels, arrow keys move without editing, type-to-edit on a cell, lookup cells with a picker (F4), validation per cell with a visible marker and a summary, totals row, paste from spreadsheet, undo, row add via Enter on the last row, keyboard shortcuts documented in a help panel.

implementation.wpf: DataGrid with custom KeyDown handling or DevExpress GridControl in edit mode (already has these behaviours).
implementation.react: AG Grid or Glide Data Grid for real spreadsheet behaviour; do not hand-roll.

title: Landing hero
use_when: Landing/campaign pages where the first screen must state the offer.
avoid_when: App screens, docs, article pages; never as the same 'headline + subtitle + two buttons + product screenshot with a gradient blob' for every product.
guidance: The hero is a specific thesis: show the real product or outcome, one headline that a user could repeat, one primary action (a second only if it is a genuinely different path), proof close by (not a logo wall by default), LCP image optimised, text contrast guaranteed, no autoplay video without a poster and reduced-motion handling. Structure varies by product: a demo, a live widget, a number, a photograph, or a form can be the hero.
source: Landing page practice; frontend-design skill calibration

title: TV sign-in: code on screen and companion device
use_when: Any TV app with accounts or subscriptions.
avoid_when: Never make remote-typed passwords the primary path.
guidance: Primary path: a short activation code (6–8 chars, no ambiguous glyphs, large 10-foot type) plus a short URL or QR code, polled until the companion device completes sign-in; the TV screen shows what to do in one sentence, the code, a 'waiting' state that is obviously alive, expiry with a regenerate action, and a secondary 'type here' fallback using the system keyboard. On success land on the profile picker; on shared TVs offer a PIN for adult profiles. Focus starts on the primary fallback button so BACK/SELECT behave predictably.

implementation.compose-tv: Poll with a coroutine and show a progress indicator; keep the code in a Text with letterSpacing; focusRequester on the fallback button.
implementation.react-native: Use TVFocusGuideView so the code area is not focusable; QR via a lightweight SVG QR component.
implementation.swiftui: tvOS: use system keyboard fallback with .focusable(); consider Apple TV's built-in Continuity Keyboard / passkeys where applicable.

source: OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (RFC 8628) UX; Android TV sign-in guidance

title: Setup / progress checklist
use_when: Multi-session onboarding where tasks can be done in any order over days (connect data, invite team, verify identity, complete profile).
avoid_when: Strictly ordered dependent steps (use a wizard) or a single setup action.
guidance: A persistent checklist with a progress summary ('3 of 6 done'), each item stating outcome, time estimate, and one action; completed items stay visible and collapsed; the list is dismissible once essentials are done and reachable again from help; items deep-link to the exact screen and return to the checklist; never block the product behind it. Announce progress changes to assistive tech; keep it out of the main content's focal position.

title: Product detail page (PDP)
use_when: Selling a physical or digital product: gallery, variants, price, availability, add-to-cart, trust and shipping information, reviews.
avoid_when: Catalog/listing pages (use list + filters) or marketing landing pages (hero + narrative).
guidance: Above the fold on every viewport: product name, price (with tabular figures and any discount stated in words), primary image, variant selectors and one add-to-cart action; variant choice is a radio group with visible labels and a disabled-but-visible state for out-of-stock options; the add-to-cart button is sticky on phones without covering focused controls; shipping, returns and stock are stated next to the price, not in a tab; the gallery has fixed aspect boxes (no layout shift), keyboard-operable thumbnails and alt text per image; reviews show the distribution and a count, and stars always have a text value; secondary actions (wishlist, share, size guide) never compete visually with add-to-cart; the size guide opens as a dialog that returns focus.

implementation.react: Radio group for variants (fieldset/legend), useId for price/availability live region, next/image or width/height for gallery boxes.
implementation.html-css: <fieldset> variants; <output aria-live="polite"> for price/availability updates; position: sticky bar with scroll-padding-bottom so focused fields stay visible.

source: Baymard Institute PDP research summaries; torture test p3-ecommerce-web (2026-09-09)

title: One-page checkout
use_when: Purchase flows with contact, shipping, payment and review on one scrolling page.
avoid_when: Multi-session or regulated flows that need a stepper with server-side validation per step.
guidance: Order summary is visible on desktop (side column) and collapsible-but-present at the top on phones with the total always shown; guest checkout first, account optional; sections in the order contact → shipping → payment → review, each with a visible heading and inline validation on blur plus a focused error summary on submit; address fields use autocomplete attributes and correct input types/IME; the pay button states the amount, is disabled only while processing (with a visible status), and is protected against double submission; trust and cost information (shipping, tax) appears before payment, never as a surprise; progress is saved locally so a reload does not lose entries.

implementation.html-css: autocomplete="shipping postal-code" etc.; inputmode="numeric" for card and postal fields; aria-describedby error links; aria-live status on the pay button.
implementation.react: Controlled form with per-field touched state; disable pay while pending and announce with role=status; persist draft in sessionStorage.

source: Baymard checkout usability research summaries; torture test p3-ecommerce-web (2026-09-09)

title: Plan comparison and billing management
use_when: Billing/plan pages: choosing or changing a plan, seat management, invoice history, payment method.
avoid_when: Public pricing marketing pages (hero + narrative) or checkout for a one-off purchase.
guidance: Plans are a radio group of equal-width cards with the current plan marked in text (not colour only), prices with tabular figures and the billing period stated, a feature list with real text (no bare check marks without labels), and one primary action per state (Upgrade / Downgrade / Current); every card is one Tab stop with a visible focus ring, arrow keys move between plans; seat management is a data table (name, role, status, last active) with row actions reachable from the keyboard and a bulk selection state; invoice history is a table with date, amount (tabular), status text + icon and a real download link (not a hover-only icon); plan changes and seat removals confirm in a dialog that states the billing consequence and returns focus; billing settings sub-navigation is a vertical list with aria-current.

implementation.nextjs: Server component for the invoice table; client radio group for plans; shadcn Dialog with returnFocus; Table with <th scope> and numeric cells using tabular-nums.
implementation.react: role=radiogroup on the plan row; roving tabindex; download as <a download> with the file name in the link text.

source: SaaS billing UX practice; torture test p3-nextjs-saas (2026-09-09)

title: Mini player / picture-in-picture state
use_when: Playback continues while the user browses (home rails, EPG, queue) on TV, or while navigating a mobile/web app.
avoid_when: Content that must not play in the background (paid live events with strict windows) or when the platform provides system PiP that the app should adopt instead.
guidance: The mini player is a single focusable/tappable region anchored to a corner (TV: bottom-right inside the safe margin, never over the focused rail; mobile: bottom above the tab bar; web: bottom-right) with the title (one line, truncated with a full title on focus), live/progress indicator and exactly two actions (expand, close); on TV, SELECT expands to the full player and BACK from the full player returns to the mini state with focus restored to the element that was focused before; playback state (playing/paused/buffering/error) is shown with an icon plus text, and the audio keeps playing while the UI is navigated; the region is excluded from the rail's D-pad focus loop except through an explicit UP/RIGHT move; never autoplay audio from a mini player on page load on web.

implementation.compose-tv: Box aligned BottomEnd with padding 48.dp; focusProperties { up/left = FocusRequester.Default }; BackHandler ordering: full player → mini → home.
implementation.compose: Use PictureInPicture params when the app is backgrounded; in-app mini via a Scaffold bottom slot above the NavigationBar.
implementation.react: Persist the media element across route changes (portal or layout-level player) so playback survives navigation.

source: Android TV / Android PiP guidance; torture test p3-android-tv-compose (2026-09-09)

title: Media details screen, resume playback and watchlist
use_when: Title/episode details, continue-watching rows, watchlist actions in a streaming or catch-up app.
avoid_when: Live-only channels without on-demand content (use the guide and player rules).
guidance: Details: the primary action is Play (or Resume with the remaining time and a Start over alternative) and it takes default focus; metadata is a short scannable block (duration, year, rating, badges as text not colour), synopsis ≤3 lines with an expander, episodes as a rail or list with progress bars and the next unwatched episode preselected; secondary actions (watchlist, trailer, more like this) sit after Play in one row. Resume: a continue-watching row shows progress on each card, resumes at the saved position, and removes finished items; entering a title from the row returns focus to that card. Watchlist: one toggle with a clear on/off state and text label, works from cards and details, and is reflected immediately in the watchlist row. Everything is reachable with D-pad UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT and BACK returns to the row that launched the details.

implementation.compose-tv: focusRequester on the Play button in the details Column; LazyRow with focusRestorer for episodes; remember the launching card key to restore focus on BACK.
implementation.swiftui: tvOS: .prefersDefaultFocus on Play inside a focusScope; NavigationStack path keeps the row/card identity for restoration.

source: Android TV design: Details and playback; Apple TV HIG: content details; blind held-out v2 media class (Phase 3)
keywords: pick up where they left off

title: On-screen keypad / keyboard for kiosks
use_when: Identify / PIN / date-of-birth / name entry on a public touch screen, with or without a tactile keypad or scanner.
avoid_when: Devices with a physical keyboard as the primary input.
guidance: Keys ≥ 64 px with ≥ 16 px gaps, one key = one accessible name ('Hyphen', 'Delete', 'Space'), the keypad is a role=group labelled by the field it edits; the value box is focusable and read back through a polite live region as it changes; a persistent format hint (not a placeholder) is tied to the field with aria-describedby and errors set aria-invalid with a specific message ('Day must be 1–31'); focus never falls to the page body after a tap (re-focus the equivalent key after a re-render); a physical keypad or scanner wedge writes into the same field (human-speed keys fill, Enter continues, bursts are treated as scans); masked entry for PINs with a visible dot per character; in accessible mode the keypad and value sit in the reach zone (lower part of the screen).

implementation.html-css: <div role="group" aria-labelledby=…> of <button> keys; <output aria-live="polite"> for the value; keydown handler distinguishes scanner bursts by inter-key interval.

source: WCAG 2.5.8 target size, 4.1.3 status messages, 3.3.1 error identification; ADA reach ranges; real projects p3-kiosk-pharmacy and p4-09 (2026-09-09)

title: Photo capture field (take, retake, replace, remove)
use_when: Forms that attach one or more photos: inspections, claims, returns, deliveries, ID capture.
avoid_when: Desktop-only forms (use a file picker with drag-and-drop) or single decorative avatars.
guidance: The field shows the thumbnails as one row of ≥ 96 dp tiles plus an 'Add photo' tile; each thumbnail is a single target that opens a sheet with Retake (camera, replaces in place), Replace from gallery, Remove (confirm only if it is the last required photo); state per photo (uploading, pending sync, failed with retry) is shown on the tile with icon + text; the camera permission is primed before the first capture and refusal leaves a way to continue; capture never loses other field values (persist the draft before opening the camera); images are downscaled for upload and the original is kept until sync succeeds; the field is announced as 'Photos, 2 of 4 added' and each tile as 'Photo 1, retake or remove'. Tapping a thumbnail opens the photo full-size (zoomable, previous/next, retake/remove) so the capture can be checked before submitting.

implementation.flutter: image_picker with maxWidth; a ListView of 104 dp tiles; showModalBottomSheet for actions; persist the form state in the notifier before launching the camera.
implementation.compose: ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture + PickVisualMedia; ModalBottomSheet; rememberSaveable for the draft.

title: TV side sheet / chooser
use_when: Choosing subtitles, audio tracks, quality, playback speed or a profile from inside the player or a rail screen.
avoid_when: More than two levels deep; more than ~8 options per column without grouping; opening it must not pause auto-hide logic incorrectly.
guidance: A right-hand sheet (~600 dp) over a scrim; columns of radio rows; first focus lands on the current value; selected state is a fill + check + semantics distinct from the focus ring; SELECT applies immediately; BACK closes and returns focus to the button that opened it; show the current choice next to the button when closed; include an Off row and a 'no tracks' text state; player controls stay hidden while the sheet is open.

title: Full-size photo viewer
use_when: Photos attached to a report, an order, a claim or a listing must be checked at full size (in the field, with gloves, in sunlight).
avoid_when: Never let thumbnails be the only view; never decode full-resolution images for thumbnails.
guidance: Thumbnails at least 2-up and decoded at display size × DPR; tap opens a full-screen viewer route (system back closes it) with pinch/double-tap zoom plus an explicit zoom button, labelled previous/next, retake/remove in the bar, dark chrome with high-contrast controls, and 48 dp targets; keep the report state when returning.
